title: Key focus 2026-11-24 — window Nov 20-23 vs Nov 13-19 (12 keys; Roblox keys only in the Direct3D cohort check)

sections.h: Read first: cohort verdicts use session-time evidence, not the verified outcome
items: Uber SMS - Direct3D renderer with a non-Windows UA: ATTACK GETTING THROUGH (5/6 indicators). ~26k/day -> ~600k/day, does not follow the key's daily rhythm, platform/fake-fingerprint anomalies on ~48%, top JA4 t13d3013h1_1d37bd780c83 claims 'Chrome Mobile 158' but offers only HTTP/1.1 with 30 ciphers (an HTTP library, not a phone) - and ~45% of it verifies. This is the clearest case of a high pass rate meaning the attack works, not that it is legitimate.

gtop100 - dishort300 + dp-spoof + ja4-dict1: ATTACK GETTING THROUGH (3/6), not the FP I first called it. ~680 sessions per IP, 90% hosting/proxy, 55% one ASN (208172), flat around the clock, one JA4 that is not a browser (HTTP/1.1 only, unknown 18-cipher stack) claiming Chrome 154 - and 83% verifies. Steady since before the window, so it is an ongoing scraper/farm, not a new spike.

Amazon IDS - Direct3D renderer with an iPadOS/iOS/Android UA: attack, ~20% getting through (4/6) - not testers. ~120-170k/day (already there before the window), 35% hosting/proxy, ~7 sessions/IP, 273 UA claims over 42 JA4s, and 67% of it on JA4 t12d280700_b75078996b15: TLS 1.2, NO ALPN, 28 ciphers - an HTTP library claiming Mobile Safari. My earlier 'ambiguous at 35% verified' call was wrong.

Hcom OTP + Login - os-spoof + pagebio: attack, blocked (3/6). 100% hosting/proxy on one ASN (210644), ~10-14 sessions/IP, runs against the key's rhythm, and the 'Mobile Safari 17' JA4 has Safari's cipher set but 15 extensions (real Safari 17 sends 13-14): a TLS impersonation library. 76% / 52% of each key's traffic in the window, 0% verified.

Blizzard ROW Support - webgl + dp-spoof: attack, blocked (3/6): SwiftShader on 94%, ~190 sessions per device id, flat around the clock, 0% verified. Amazon IDS - ends-cl: suspicious (2/6): 47% from one ASN (200373), language mismatch 70%, 19% verified - watch.

Uber SMS - ends-cl combination: attack, mostly blocked (4/6): 0.7M -> 4.6M/day, ~14 sessions/IP, platform mismatch 53%, ~1% verified. The real Chrome TLS stack (JA4 consistent) means real automated Chrome, caught by the other signals.

Roblox Signup - Direct3D with a non-Windows UA: suspicious, mostly blocked (~58k/day, 7.7 sessions/IP, off-rhythm, 11% verified). Uber Account Management - ends-cl: suspicious, partly getting through (off-rhythm, language mismatch on 70%, 66% verified) - worth a closer look rather than an FP call.

Uber SMS - mobile GPU with a Windows UA: looks like real users (follows the daily rhythm, spread out, normal TLS) despite being new - likely a client/WebView change; low pass rate means the challenge is hard for them, so do NOT add pressure on this signal alone.

Uber SMS (Key 1): volumetric and growing. All sessions 12.6M/day -> 19M, 26M, 21M, 35M, 70M (Nov 18-23); verified share 55% -> 19%. The ends-cl combination flags ~4.5M/day at ~1% verified. One JA4 (t13d1517h2_8daaf6152771_cb7bf5808d99, 'Chrome 148' with 51 different UA claims, mostly Vietnam) carries 4.35M flagged sessions in 2 days at 0% verified, plus a 12-fingerprint rotation group (~5.5k each, 8% verified). New in the window: no WebGL renderer 2% -> 10% (peak 31%), navigator.platform != OS 1% -> 7% (peak 24%), JS UA != HTTP UA header 0.3% -> 2.6%, renderer inconsistent with OS. Mostly blocked, but at 70M/day even 1% getting through is ~700k sessions. The charts show the tracked combinations peaked on Nov 20-22 (ends-cl 9.1M on Nov 20) and fell back, while total traffic kept climbing to ~67-70M on Nov 23 with verified flat at ~13M/day: most of the newest volume is NOT matched by any tracked combination (it is being stopped by something else). Worth a discovery pass on this key to find the signal combination behind the Nov 22-23 growth.

Blizzard ROW Support Site (Key 3): bot wave with rotating TLS fingerprints. Up to 366k/day (Nov 18) and 332k (Nov 23) at 26-29% verified. Language != Accept-Language 6% -> 30% (peak 46%), sec-ch-ua != UA version 1.5% -> 16%, SwiftShader software renderer 6% -> 19% (now the key's most common renderer). The webgl + dp-spoof combination (28k/day) is 15 JA4s with the same cipher set and ~5.3k each, all 'Chrome 146' with sec-ch-ua disagreeing on 96-100%, 0% verified, spread across PL/GB/CH/IT/NL - blocked.

Hcom OTP (Key 7) and Hcom Login (Key 6), Expedia: attack Nov 16-22, ended Nov 23. OTP went from ~30k/day to 150-220k/day at 16-23% verified, back to 38k at 98% verified on Nov 23. The os-spoof + pagebio combination there is one JA4 (t13d2015h2_a09f3c656075_c258b721e490) claiming Mobile Safari 17, 100% from one ASN (210644, GB), 0% verified; ~77-80% of the key's sessions were hosting/proxy IPs with platform and WebGL renderer inconsistent with the OS. Same JA4 and ASN on Login. Blocked; the Nov 23 'drop' is the attack stopping, not an outage.

Blizzard ROW Registration (Key 2): ~54k/day -> 5.3k (Nov 20), 1.1k (Nov 21), 182 (Nov 22), 13.6k (Nov 23, partial recovery). No attribute anomaly; Blizzard Login (Key 5, ~150k/day, ~59% verified) and Support were up as normal. The registration page stopped calling the key - confirm with Blizzard.

Uber Account Management (Key 2): the key itself is ~0.9-1M/day at 97-99% verified; the ends-cl cohort on it is now 'suspicious, partly getting through' (see the cohort card) - earlier 'possible FP' call withdrawn.
Amazon IDS: hosting/proxy share fell (30% -> 22%); 174k flagged in 2 days from one JA4 on one ASN (200373, US) at 24% verified - concentrated but partly verified.

BofA CashPro: one 1M burst on Nov 13 at 0% verified (blocked); ~300k/day at ~90% verified since; weekend dips are normal for this key. Highlight AI: 92k burst Nov 13 at 3% verified, ~10k/day at ~55% since. OKCupid Registration: 0% verified, 1-4k/day, no data after Nov 20.
CAPI 4.8.0 rolled out across most keys around Nov 20 (4.7.0 -> 4.8.0), so a CAPI change to 4.8.0 is a release, not an anomaly. BofA CashPro stays on 4.6.1, gtop100 on 3.7.2, Blizzard Login on 2.18.1.
The timezone check had a case bug in this run (asia/seoul vs Asia/Seoul) and is left out; fixed for the next run.
Drop check now ignores normal weekend dips (same weekday last week also low).
